results.title: River embankment collapses in Odisha's Jajpur; villagers evacuated as Baitarani crosses danger mark
results.description: Jajpur: A portion of the embankment of the Kani river, a branch of the Baitarani, collapsed at Patana village under Tarpada panchayat in Odisha 's Jajpur district early on Sunday. The embankment collapsed at a location in front of the village as floodwater continued to flow strongly through the river. According to locals, a tree standing along the edge of the embankment was first swept away by the water current during the night. Soon after, the soil began giving way. At around 5 am, another section of the Kani River embankment at Patana collapsed completely. The damaged stretch is around 30 feet long and 15 feet wide. Following the incident, locals and officials of the Water Resources Department started immediate repair work to prevent further damage. However, continuous rainfall since the night has hampered the restoration efforts. Fire Services personnel have started evacuating villagers to a safer location on the Baitarani river embankment. Meanwhile, the Baitarani river was flowing above the danger mark at 7 am. The water level was recorded at 18.38 metres, against the danger mark of 18.33 metres.

results.title: Rescuers dig through rubble and landslides after Indonesia quake kills 47
results.description: At least 24 people died in Manggarai regency and 17 in neighboring East Manggarai, with additional fatalities reported in Sikka, Ngada and Ende regencies, the National Disaster Management Agency said. Rescuers were still searching for villagers feared buried beneath landslides triggered by the quake across six regencies on Flores, a predominantly Catholic island in Muslim-majority Indonesia.

results.title: TVK govt’s first 100 days: Welfare push, investment gains and mounting challenges
results.description: Chennai, Aug 16 (IANS) The TVK government led by C. Joseph Vijay completes 100 days in office on Monday, marking a political shift in Tamil Nadu after more than five decades of alternating rule by the DMK and the AIADMK. TVK, a young political party, won the Assembly election in April and formed the government on May 10. Vijay took the oath with nine ministers. The Cabinet was expanded with 23 ministers on May 21 and two more the following day. Immediately after assuming office, Vijay signed three key files. These provided 200 free units of electricity every two months to domestic consumers using up to 500 units, proposed a Singappen Special Task Force for women’s safety and established 65 anti-narcotics units. The government closed 717 TASMAC liquor outlets near educational institutions and places of worship. It raised the dearness allowance for government employees from 58 to 60 per cent, ordered the renovation of Amma canteens and announced the waiver of crop loans of up to Rs 50,000 for marginal farmers. During his visit to New Delhi on May 27, CM Vijay met Prime Minister Narendra Modi and submitted demands concerning the Mekedatu dam dispute and the problems faced by Tamil Nadu fishermen. On June 9, he launched the Singappen force and later announced a gold-ring scheme for babies born in government hospitals. The revised Budget unveiled several welfare measures, including eight-gram gold coins and silk clothing for brides, 70,000 concrete houses to replace huts, modern bicycles for Class 11 students and laptops for government college students. State Finance Minister Maria Wilson said 125 election promises had been incorporated into the Budget. For the TVK government, Industry has emerged as a major focus. The government says 104 agreements have attracted investments exceeding Rs 1 lakh crore during its first 100 days. At the Vetri Tamil Nadu Investors’ Conclave alone, 97 agreements worth Rs 67,452 crore were signed, with the potential to create 1.07 lakh jobs across 23 districts. However, the administration faces opposition criticism over law and order, sexual offences, power disruptions and poor waste management. Its inexperienced ministers have also had to counter DMK and AIADMK legislators in the Assembly. Despite these challenges, the government has projected an image of administrative urgency, welfare expansion and vigilance against corruption. Its early record appears promising, but implementation of its announcements and investments will determine whether the first 100 days become the foundation for lasting change. --IANS aal/dpb
